tip: walk BEFORE breakfast. your dog stops being weird around 11am.
if your dog can't sit at home, they can't sit on a walk. start where it's quiet.
mental work tires dogs out faster than physical. one frozen kong equals a long walk.
if you can hear yourself yelling, your dog already stopped listening.
the leash is a conversation, not a steering wheel.
reactivity isn't aggression. it's panic in a small body.
treat where the behavior was, not where you are.
the threshold is the distance where your dog notices but hasn't lost their mind.
predictability beats discipline. dogs love routine more than they love treats.
if the cue isn't working, it's the cue. say it once. then help.
the dog isn't being stubborn. they're overwhelmed, confused, or both.
your couch is fine. your dog isn't ruining it. the rule is the rule.
if the recall fails outdoors, the recall failed indoors first.
every dog has a default direction. learn theirs before you correct it.
puppies don't generalize. teach 'sit' in five rooms before you call it learned.
if the bark gets louder when you yell, you taught them to bark louder.
the best fix for chewing is a better chew. the second-best is a tired dog.
groomers aren't magicians. teach the brush at home first.
if the dog freezes, the dog is talking. listen.
rewards build behavior. corrections suppress it. behavior shows up again. suppression doesn't last.
